screens.speaker: rosa
screens.text: Let's start with the moment that comes up most.
screens.question: Where do Mom's repeated questions usually reach you?

screens.setup: You're at work. Mom calls for the third time today:
screens.line: When are you coming on Saturday?
screens.question: What would you say?

answers.text: Saturday morning, around ten. Write it down so you remember.
Mom, I told you already. Saturday. I'm at work.
You're wondering when I'll come. I'll call you before I leave, so you don't have to keep track. What are you doing right now?

screens.afterChoice: You can try another answer to compare.

screens.title: Each time feels like the first time to her.
screens.body: Mom isn't testing you, and isn't doing it on purpose. The memory of asking fades, but the feeling behind the question stays. To her, the question really is new.

miniTask.question: What might be behind the question?

screens.title: Answer the feeling first. Keep it short and the same.
screens.body: Use the three steps: notice the feeling, reassure, offer something to do. Then say it the same short way each time. Long explanations are harder for her to follow and tiring for you.

steps.label: Reassure
steps.example: We have plenty of time. I'll tell you when it's time.

steps.label: Offer something to do
steps.example: Want to help me with the tea?

miniTask.question: Which reply follows all three steps?

options.label: It's at 2, like I said. The doctor just wants to check on you, nothing to worry about, and then we'll go home.
You're wondering about it. I've got it covered. Want to fold these towels with me?

screens.title: Make the answer easy to find, and don't announce plans too early.
bullets: Ask her to keep a note by the phone with the next visit: "Saturday. I'll call before I leave."
Mention plans closer to the time. A visit announced days ahead gives the worry more time to grow.
screens.patternTip: Look for a pattern: does it happen at a certain time of day, or after something specific?

screens.title: The fifth time is the hardest.
screens.body: Feeling frustrated is normal. It doesn't make you a bad daughter or son. What helps is a small reset before you answer.

miniTask.question: Pick your reset for next time:

options.label: One slow breath before I answer
Step away for a minute, if it's safe
